Overcoming a lack of possession (45%), they completed strongly (81%) to make 9.7m per carry and 5 line breaks. Their missed tackles (37) did give their opponents too many chances; conceding 30 points and 5 line breaks must be improved upon heading into next season. This aside, some of the efforts displayed by players highlights that positivity still exists within this team.

Fighting back strongly, they ended the game with a 22-14 loss; they will take confidence in keeping their opponents scoreless in the second half. This was achieved by controlling possession (56%) and having a high completion rate (85%), managing the conditions positively. NRL Judiciary: Young, Frizell, Cogger banned until finals
Knights duo Dom Young and Tyson Frizell won't play again until the finals after both copped one-game bans for Dangerous Contact offences after the loss to Manly.
Young's hip drop tackle on Tolu Koula in the 33rd minute was classified as a Grade 2 offence and carried a one-game ban with an early guilty plea.

items.body_excerpt:
Finals may not be on the line for last year’s two grand final sides when they meet on Thursday night , but Andrew Johns and Brad Fittler expect there to be plenty of feeling in the clash between the Broncos and the Storm due to a narrative that has underpinned the rivalry between the two clubs for decades.
The Broncos won last year’s decider to make it two from two in grand finals against the Storm, the other coming in 2006 when Wayne Bennett masterminded a victory over Craig Bellamy in a clash involving some of the greatest players of this century.
Harry Grant and Cameron Munster. Getty Images
While the Broncos have clear bragging rights from that point-of-view, the Storm have an amazing overall record against the Queensland powerhouse, winning 41 of their 63 matches played.
In games played in Brisbane, the Storm leads the head-to-head 20-9.
It’s a phenomenal record given that the Broncos have had their fair share of success since the Storm entered the competition in 1998.
The theory goes that part of the reason Melbourne save some of their best performances for the Broncos at Suncorp Stadium is the scattering of Queenslanders in the Storm system, many of whom were overlooked at one time or another by the Broncos.
It is folklore that all-time greats Cameron Smith , Billy Slater and Cooper Cronk fell into the laps of the Storm courtesy of dud recruitment calls made by the Broncos.
Read more
Walsh ‘like’ deleted as fear of Broncos revolt laid bare
Johns is adamant that Melbourne still goes to Brisbane with a “bee in the bonnet” due to the players in the current squad who had a similar experience.
“They just hate them because they got brushed,” Fittler said on Wide World of Sports’ NRL Tips .
“Cameron, Billy, Cooper...”
The list keeps growing - and it’s enough to give any Broncos fan a headache.
“And this time they’re going to have (Cameron) Munster, Harry Grant, (Trent) Loiero ... so yeah, there’s a bee in the bonnet for them.”
Both Fittler and Johns are tipping the Storm to win a match that at the start of the season most would have expected to be a preview to the pointy end of the finals series.
Adam Reynolds and Michael Maguire after Brisbane’s premiership victory last year. Getty Images
Instead it is a clash of two fallen giants, with the Storm 11th on the ladder and out of the race to make the eight, while the Broncos only avoided being dragged into wooden spoon calculations thanks to an upset win over the Raiders in round 25 and have this week faced a storm of their own making after mishandling Adam Reynolds’ retirement .
While neither team can make the eight, there will be plenty of feeling in the game and it will draw additional interest due to the trial of a new rule, with the team that concedes a try to determine whether they kick off or receive at the following restart.

items.body_excerpt:
‘Perfect time to trial it’: Storm has no issue with being the guinea pigs for major rule change, but one mystery remains
The Storm has no problems being the guinea pigs for a major rule change on Thursday, but mystery surrounds one key element.
The Storm has no objections to being involved in Thursday night’s kick-off rule trial and will have an open mind to the experiment when they face the Broncos just a year after the teams met in a grand final.
The high stakes of last year’s decider have gone with Brisbane down in 15th spot on the ladder, while the Storm has missed the finals for the first time since 2010.
The teams were told on Monday that they would be guinea pigs for the new rule, which was floated in the pre-season at a meeting involving some of the biggest coaches in the game.
Brisbane and Melbourne have gone from playing in a grand final to having new rules trialled in their game because neither side will make the top eight. Picture: Cameron Spencer/Getty Images
Under the proposed change, that team that concedes a try, penalty goal or field goal will have the choice of kicking off or receiving the ball from the restart, instead of them booting the ball back to the side that scored.
The option is designed to prevent one team from having a significant run of possession that could lead to an avalanche of points.
Thursday’s trial has received mixed support but is a good chance for the NRL to test out its new rule with two powerhouse clubs.
Others you may like
“We don’t have an issue with it,” Storm general manager of football Frank Ponissi told the NewsWire
“As a club, earlier in the year we would have opposed the rule being brought in, but we certainly support the trial of it.
“I think the NRL should be congratulated on the way they’ve gone about it because I think the correct way of doing it is by trialling it in such a high-profile game.
Frank Ponissi says the Storm don’t have plans for how to use the new rule. Picture: Josh Chadwick/Getty Images
“While both teams can’t make the finals, both are quality teams and it’s a prime-time TV game, so it’s the perfect time to trial such a thing.
“We certainly didn’t have any objection to being involved.”
It’s unclear whether a team would ever choose to kick-off under the new rules and forfeit possession, but there could be advantages if it’s windy or rainy and they feel like they can earn territory by kicking long.
“We don’t know (what we’ll do), it’s all new to us,” Ponissi said.
More Coverage
“We’re going in with a very open mind and will see how it goes.
“We’re not having any premeditated notions of ‘we’ll do this or we’ll do that’. We’re just going in with an open mind and seeing how it evolves.
“Maybe when you do it a second time, that’s when you might do things differently, but it’s going to be new to us.”
